title: EMERGENCY RESPIRATORY MEDICINE: EXAM CLINICAL GUIDE
summary: An exhaustive clinical resource covering the diagnosis, investigation, and management of life-threatening respiratory conditions including Acute Severe Asthma, COPD Exacerbations, Pneumonia, and Tension Pneumothorax. Prepared for FRCS (Glasg) Exam preparation by Waleed Badr.

sections.title: Asthma Investigations & Initial Treatment (ABC)
content: Investigations: Peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR)
Investigations: ABG (high CO2, low O2 [<90%] + low pH)
Investigations: CXR, FBC & U&E
Call for help
Sit patient up & do not sedate
ABC: Ensure patent airway
Give oxygen 100% & secure IV line

sections.title: First-Line Asthma Pharmacotherapy
content: Step 1: Salbutamol (B2-agonist) 5 mg (or terbutaline 10 mg) plus ipratropium bromide 0.5 mg nebulized with oxygen
Step 2: Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV or prednisolone 30 mg PO or both if very ill
Step 3: Monitor oxygen saturation (pulse oximeter), heart rate and respiratory rate
Step 4: CXR to exclude pneumothorax

sections.title: If Asthma Not Improving: Escalation Protocol
content: After 30 min: Repeat salbutamol every 15min or 10mg continuously per hour
Give Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV or prednisolone 30 mg PO if not already given
Next Step: Consider aminophylline (5 mg/kg IVI over 20 min) OR give salbutamol IVI (3 – 20 ug/min)
Final Escalation: Consider transfer to ICU to intubate, give adrenaline and 500 mL colloid IVI

sections.title: Asthma Recovery & Weaning Protocol
content: Wean and stop aminophylline over 12 – 24h
Switch to inhaled B-agonist bronchodilator and steroids
Continue to monitor PEFR for 24h: Aim for rate > 75% of predicted or best with diurnal variability < 25%
Warning: Beware of early morning dips in PEFR
Look for cause of acute exacerbation

sections.title: Acute Exacerbation of COPD
content: Common in winter & triggered by viral or bacterial infections
Presentations: Increased cough, breathlessness or wheeze with decreased exercise capacity
History: Ask about usual treatment (home oxygen), smoking and exercise capacity
Investigations: PEFR, ABG, CXR, ECG
Lab Tests: Blood culture (if pyrexial) & sputum culture
Management Step 1: Look for the cause e.g. infection or pneumothorax

sections.title: COPD: Controlled Oxygen Therapy
content: Don’t leave patients hypoxic
Risk: Patients relying on hypoxic drive; too much oxygen may lead to reduced respiratory rate, hypercapnia, and fall in conscious level
If CO2 retention: Start with 24 – 28% O2. Reassess after 30 min
Aim: Raise O2 above 8.0KPa with a rise in CO2 < 1.5KPa
If no retention: Use 28-40% O2 but still monitor and repeat ABG

sections.title: COPD Medical Management Steps
content: 1. Nebulized bronchodilator (salbutamol 5mg/4h & ipratropium 500ug/6h)
2. Hydrocortisone 200mg IV & oral prednisolone 30-40mg
3. Antibiotics if evidence of infection
4. Physiotherapy to aid sputum expectoration
5. If no response: consider IV aminophylline
6. If still no response: consider nasal intermittent positive pressure ventilation (NIPPV)
7. Intubation and ventilation: Consider if pH decreases and CO2 increases
8. Respiratory stimulant: Doxapram (short term only, for patients not suitable for mechanical ventilation)

sections.title: Long-Term Management of Stable COPD
content: Stop smoking, encourage exercise, proper nutrition, weight reduction
Influenza vaccination
Medications: Short acting B2-agonist, ipratropium and corticosteroid inhalations (according to severity)
Consider long term oxygen therapy
Surgery: Indicated for recurrent pneumothorax or isolated bullous disease
Social/Psych: Assess social circumstances/support; Identify and treat depression
Travel: Air travel is hazardous if O2 saturation is low; check availability of O2

sections.title: Pneumonia: Definition & Incidence
content: Definition: An infection of the lung parenchyma
Incidence: 12 per 1000 adults
Mortality rate: 10%

sections.title: Pneumonia Organisms: The Full List
sections.content: Strept. pneumoniae (commonest 60-75%); Mycoplasma pneumoniae (5-18%); Others: Staph. aureus, Haemophilus influenzae, Legionella & Chlamydia psittaci, G-ve bacilli e.g. Pseudomonas (often hospital-acquired or immunocompromised).

rows: Signs of consolidation: diminished expansion, dull percussion note
Increased tactile vocal fremitus/vocal resonance, bronchial breathing

content.explanation: C: Confusion; U: Urea > 7mmol/L; R: Respiratory rate ≥ 30/min; B: BP < 90/60; 65: Age ≥ 65

sections.title: CURB-65 Scoring Actions
content: Score 0-1: Home treatment if possible
Score 2: Hospital therapy
Score ≥ 3: Severe pneumonia

sections.title: Pneumonia Management: ABC & Investigations
content: A: Adequate ventilation (may need intubation)
B: Oxygenation
C: Circulation (IV line, treat hypotension & shock)
Investigations: CXR, ABG, FBC, U&E, LFT, CRP, blood culture
Advanced Investigations: Aspiration of pleural fluid for culture & bronchoscopy (if immunocompromised)

rows: Pericarditis, Myocarditis, Cholestatic jaundice, Renal failure

sections.title: Tension Pneumothorax: EMERGENCY
content: MEDICAL EMERGENCY: Requires immediate relief
CRITICAL: Do not delay management for obtaining a CXR
Pathophysiology: Air inside pleural space has no route to escape, pushing mediastinum to opposite side, kinking/compressing great veins
Risk: Unless air is rapidly removed, cardio respiratory arrest will occur

sections.title: Causes of Pneumothorax
content: Primary (Spontaneous): Especially in young thin men
Secondary: Underlying disease (Asthma, COPD, TB, Pneumonia, Lung abscess, Fibrosis, Carcinoma)
Trauma
Iatrogenic: Subclavian CVP line insertion, Pleural aspiration/biopsy, Percutaneous liver biopsy, +ve pressure ventilation

rows: Trachea deviated away from affected side

sections.title: Management Step 1: Aspiration
content: 1. Infilterative anaesthesia
2. Insert large bore (14-16 G) cannula (venflon) into 2nd intercostal space, mid-clavicular line
3. Connect to 3-way tap and 50mL 0.9% saline
4. Aspirate up to 2.5 litres of air
5. Request CXR to confirm resolution
6. If successful: Repeat CXR after 24h to exclude recurrence

sections.title: Management Step 2: Chest (Intercostal) Drain
content: Insert in 4th – 6th intercostal space, anterior to mid-axillary line
Use small tube unless blood/pus present
Removal: 24h after lung re-expanded & air leak stopped (bubbling stops)
Removal technique: Done during expiration or a Valsalva manoeuvre
Failed expansion: If failed within 48h, suction or surgery required

sections.title: Surgical Consultation & Long-term Advice
content: Request surgical advice if: Bilateral pneumothorax
Request surgical advice if: Lung fails to expand after drain insertion
Request surgical advice if: 2 or more previous episodes on same side
Request surgical advice if: History of pneumothorax on opposite side
Travel Advice: Avoid air travel for 6 weeks after normal CXR
Activity Advice: Diving should be permanently avoided
